title: Copro-diagnostic molecular method for detection of herpetofauna infecting nematodes
author: Lucas G. Huggins
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i32cgqe
materials: DNA was extracted from a starting faecal quantity of 10-200 mg (depending on obtainable amount) using the QIAamp® Fast DNA Stool Mini Kit (Qiagen) under aseptic conditions using the manufacturer’s protocol alongside the following modifications.

A disruption step was included in which the faecal samples were added to 1 ml of InhibitEx buffer followed by bead-beating using 4 mm diameter borosilicate glass beads (Sigma) placed within an Eppendorf Safelock 2 ml test tube. Samples were then bead-beaten in a Retsch MM400 mixer mill (Derbyshire, UK) at 30 Hz for between 5 – 10 min with regular movement of the samples between the pockets of the arm cradles to ensure a consistent beating across all samples.
Samples were vortexed for one minute and then incubated and shaken in an Eppendorf Thermomixer C (Stevenage, UK) at 45⁰C and 67 g for between 1 – 2 hours.

PCRs were prepared in aseptic conditions with all consumables UV sterilised, mastermixes were made on ice. PCRs were typically 25 µl in volume comprising: 10.88 µl of Mili-Q water, 2.5 mM PCR buffer, 3.5 mM Mg, 0.5 µM dNTPs, 0.024 U/µl FastStart Taq DNA Polymerase (Roche, Sussex, UK), 0.5 µM of both forward and reverse primers and 0.5 µl BSA (100X) (New England Biolabs Inc., Hitchin UK).

PCR product amplicons were cleaned using a MiniElute® PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen), with slight modifications to the manufacturer’s protocol. Cleaned DNA was eluted in 10 µl of autoclaved Milli-Q water for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Digest samples with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample with Proteinase K for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Elute DNA from purification column
steps.instruction: Perform two elution steps: first elute with 100 µl buffer AE for 20 min with centrifugation; then elute with 50 µl buffer AE for 15 min with centrifugation.

steps.title: Store DNA at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Keep DNA samples chilled at 4 °C when not in use.

steps.title: Prepare PCR reaction mix
steps.instruction: Use 5 µl or 10 µl of faecal DNA per reaction (faecal extracts 5–100 ng/µl, tissue extracts 10–50 ng/µl). Add Nem27 primers (Nem1217F: CGN BCC GRA CAC YGT RAG; Nem1619: GGA AAY AAT TDC AAT TCC CKR TCC) to amplify a 402 bp fragment of the 18S rRNA gene.

steps.title: Run PCR thermal cycling
steps.instruction: Thermal cycle: 94 °C 5 min initial denaturation; 35 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 54 °C 30 s (annealing can be raised to 62–64 °C), 72 °C 1 min; final extension 72 °C 10 min.

steps.title: Perform agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 % agarose gel with TBE buffer and 0.5–2 µl GelGreen stain. Load each lane with 3 µl PCR product, 2 µl blue loading buffer, and 1 µl Hyperladder 1 kb. Run gel in a RunOne electrophoresis cell at 45 V for 30–80 min.

steps.title: Image gels
steps.instruction: Mount gel on a PrepOne Sapphire illuminator with a PI-1002 filter and camera hood, then photograph the gel.

steps.title: Prepare purified PCR product for sequencing
steps.instruction: Adjust cleaned PCR product to 10–40 ng/µl, add 4 pmol of a single primer, and bring the volume to 10 µl with Milli‑Q water. Submit samples for Sanger sequencing using Big Dye 3.1 chemistry on an ABI 3100 Genetic Analyzer.

steps.title: Edit and assemble sequence traces
steps.instruction: In BioEdit, trim low‑quality regions from forward and reverse traces, then align the complementary sequences using ClustalW to obtain the full amplicon sequence.

steps.title: Identify species via BLAST
steps.instruction: Query the assembled sequence against the GenBank nucleotide BLAST database to determine the species origin.
